No proof of dowry ha*assment ‘Soon Before’ death, Allahabad High Court acquits husband and in-laws

The Allahabad High Court has acquitted a husband and his relatives in a 35 year-old dowry death case, holding that the prosecution failed to establish that the woman was subjected to dowry-related cruelty or harassment “soon before” her death.

The woman had died in 1991 after her body was recovered from a well near her matrimonial home. Her family alleged dowry harassment, including a demand for a scooter. However, the High Court noted that the alleged scooter demand related to nearly four years before her death and had not been mentioned in the FIR or statements recorded during investigation.

The Court stressed that before the statutory presumption of dowry death can arise under Section 113-B of the Evidence Act, the prosecution must first establish the foundational fact that the woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment connected with dowry soon before her death.

The High Court also found serious gaps in the allegation that the woman had been murdered and her body thrown into the well. Medical evidence indicated that her head injury could have resulted from a fall into the well, while the prosecution had failed to establish the alleged manner or place of murder.

The Court further criticised the trial court for concluding that the accused had committed murder even though Section 302 IPC was neither included in the chargesheet nor framed as a charge, describing this approach as erroneous in law.

Finding that the prosecution had failed to prove the charges beyond reasonable doubt, the High Court set aside the convictions and acquitted the husband and his relatives of all charges.
comment: The judgment also highlights how delay impacts evidence quality in matrimonial offences; preserving contemporaneous complaints and medical or witness records becomes critical for both sides.
